evidence_boundary: This ledger records a source-level semantic review of lessons, worked answers, case studies, exercises, worksheets, rubrics, and lab guides. It verifies named mechanisms against bounded primary or official sources, distinguishes normative course contracts, and does not turn synthetic examples into production measurements.

claims.claim: Start with the journey and the change: workload, percentile, useful work, environment, comparison, and time window. Then list mechanisms that could produce it. For every mechanism, predict a combination of signals and a falsifier. Collection follows the ledger; available dashboards do not choose the question.
source_sections: Read Summary, Metrics, In Practice, and Other Methodologies; build a USE table and name two gaps.

claims.claim: Metrics aggregate repeated measurements. Logs preserve event detail. Traces preserve a sampled causal path. Profiles attribute resource use to code. Each signal loses information differently, so correlation is designed rather than assumed.

claims.claim: A CPU profile attributes execution to call stacks. Deterministic profiling records calls and elapsed time but adds instrumentation overhead; sampling profiles approximate where execution spends time with different bias. An allocation profile attributes created or retained memory to sites. Neither RSS nor total allocated bytes alone proves a leak.
source_sections: Read the introduction, instant user manual, and limitations; record what deterministic profiling measures and how its overhead changes the evidence boundary.
